question: What must a vessel operator have on board and available for inspection whenever a registered vessel is operated in Georgia?
choice_b: A copy of the boat's purchase receipt only
choice_c: The Certificate of Boat Registration (pocket-sized plastic card)
choice_d: Nothing needs to be on board if the decals are displayed
explanation: The Certificate of Boat Registration, a pocket-sized plastic card, must be on board and available for inspection by an enforcement officer whenever the vessel is operated.
source_note: Handbook of Georgia Boating Laws and Responsibilities, 'Registering Your Vessel'

question: Which of these vessels is EXEMPT from Georgia's boat registration requirement?
choice_a: Any vessel with an outboard motor of 10 horsepower or more
choice_b: Any vessel used exclusively for water-skiing
choice_d: Canoes, kayaks, rowboats, and rubber rafts that have no mechanical propulsion
explanation: Registration exemptions include sailboats under 12 feet, canoes/kayaks/rowboats/rubber rafts with no mechanical propulsion, vessels used exclusively on private ponds or lakes, and out-of-state vessels using Georgia waters 60 days or less.
source_note: Handbook of Georgia Boating Laws and Responsibilities, 'Registering Your Vessel'

question: How must a Georgia registration number be displayed on the bow of a vessel?
choice_a: Painted, applied as a decal, or otherwise affixed to both sides of the bow, reading left to right, in at least 3-inch-high block letters that contrast with the background
choice_b: Handwritten in pencil on a removable placard
choice_c: Displayed only on the stern, never the bow
choice_d: In any font size as long as it is legible from land
explanation: The registration number must be painted, decaled, or otherwise affixed to both sides of the bow, read left to right, be at least 3 inches high in block letters, and contrast with the background color.
source_note: Handbook of Georgia Boating Laws and Responsibilities, 'Registering Your Vessel'

question: How long is a Georgia Certificate of Boat Registration valid, and when does it expire?
choice_a: 1 year, expiring exactly on the purchase anniversary
choice_b: 3 years, expiring on the last day of the owner's month of birth
choice_c: 10 years, with no expiration tied to the owner
explanation: A Georgia Certificate of Boat Registration is valid for 3 years and expires on the last day of the owner's month of birth.
source_note: Handbook of Georgia Boating Laws and Responsibilities, 'How to Apply For or Renew Your Vessel's Registration'

question: Within how many days must a vessel owner notify the DNR Boat Registration Office of a change of address or sale of the vessel?
explanation: If a vessel owner changes addresses or sells the vessel, they must give written notice to the DNR Boat Registration Office within 15 days of the event.
source_note: Handbook of Georgia Boating Laws and Responsibilities, 'Other Facts About Registering Your Vessel'

question: What is the registration fee for a Class 2 vessel (26 feet to less than 40 feet) for a three-year Georgia boat registration?
explanation: Georgia's three-year registration fee schedule charges $130.00 for Class 2 vessels (26 feet to less than 40 feet), compared to $25 for Class A, $60 for Class 1, and $200 for Class 3.
source_note: Handbook of Georgia Boating Laws and Responsibilities, 'Registration Fees for Three-Year Boat Registration'

question: What is the Hull Identification Number (HIN), and which vessels are required to have one?
choice_a: A unique, 12-digit number assigned by the manufacturer, required on each vessel built after 1972 to legally sell or operate it on Georgia waters
choice_b: An optional serial number that only luxury yachts must carry
choice_c: A number assigned only to vessels registered outside Georgia
choice_d: The same number as the vessel's engine serial number
explanation: The HIN is a unique 12-digit number assigned by the manufacturer, engraved in the fiberglass or on a metal plate on the transom; every vessel built after 1972 must have a valid HIN to be legally sold or operated in Georgia.
source_note: Handbook of Georgia Boating Laws and Responsibilities, 'Hull Identification Number (HIN)'

question: If a Georgia-registered vessel's owner wants to sell a used vessel that has an eTitle in the DNR system, what governs the transfer if a paper title has been created?
choice_a: The eTitle always controls, and paper titles are irrelevant
choice_b: The Georgia paper title becomes the controlling document and must be transferred to the new owner
choice_c: No documentation is required for a used-vessel sale
choice_d: Only a verbal agreement between buyer and seller is needed
explanation: Georgia-registered vessels have an eTitle in the DNR system, but if a paper title has been requested or created, that paper title is the controlling document and must be transferred to the new owner.
source_note: Handbook of Georgia Boating Laws and Responsibilities, 'Buying and Selling a Vessel'

question: If a vessel owner abandons or destroys their vessel, what must they do within 15 days?
choice_a: Nothing -- no report is required for abandonment
choice_b: Purchase a brand-new registration for a replacement vessel
choice_c: Report it to the DNR Boat Registration Office and surrender the Certificate of Boat Registration
choice_d: Notify the local sheriff instead of the DNR
explanation: An owner who abandons or destroys a vessel must report it to the DNR Boat Registration Office within 15 days and surrender the Certificate of Boat Registration.
source_note: Handbook of Georgia Boating Laws and Responsibilities, 'Other Facts About Registering Your Vessel'

question: May a larger recreational vessel documented by the U.S. Coast Guard (USCG) skip Georgia's numbering requirements?
choice_a: No, USCG documentation has no effect on state requirements
choice_b: Yes, and it is also exempt from displaying any Georgia decals
choice_c: USCG documentation is only available to commercial vessels
choice_d: Yes, a USCG-documented vessel is exempt from Georgia numbering requirements but must still display Georgia validation decals on the bow
explanation: A USCG-documented vessel is exempt from Georgia's numbering requirements, but it must still display the Georgia validation decals on the bow of the vessel.
source_note: Handbook of Georgia Boating Laws and Responsibilities, 'Other Facts About Registering Your Vessel'

question: What late fee applies to renew a Georgia boat registration if the certificate of number has already expired?
choice_c: There is no late fee in Georgia
explanation: A $10 late fee is applied to renew a boat registration in Georgia if the certificate of number is already expired.
source_note: Handbook of Georgia Boating Laws and Responsibilities, 'How to Apply For or Renew Your Vessel's Registration'
